intended_phases.action: Ready, lower posture, draw at low waist.
Blade tip rises from below waist to above head; settle high.
Recover, align single blade with scabbard, resheathe to ready.

prompts.front:
Create a consistent, polished 16-frame game ATTACK SPRITE SHEET of this exact reference character performing a RISING SWORD-DRAW CUT, from LOW to HIGH. True transparent alpha background, exactly4columns×4rows with16equal square cells, row-major order, NO words/numbers/panel borders, no backgrounds or floor shadows. All16 FULLBODY figures at exactly the same SCALE, fixed boot positions and baseline; generous empty space ABOVE and to the LEFT of each figure to contain the fully extended sword. Every entire blade point stays inside its own cell. Aim1280square sheet, each320cell with character body160px tall, neutral head near y128 and boot solesy288. The sword may rise above the head into the empty upper margin. Never shrink the character just to fit a raised sword.
Match the exact approved character face, head proportions and line quality in EVERY frame: long white hair, red eyes, ivory mantle/coat with leaf embroidery, charcoal uniform with red piping and silver buttons, burgundy coat lining, brown boots, dark gloves, star brooches, leather belts. Clean uniform cel color fills with restrained shadows, no mottling or noisy texture. Use the SAME face, head width and hair volume repeatedly; only a little hair-tip/coat flutter follows the strike. Natural SHORT upper arms and forearms at constant lengths, correct elbow bends, aligned wrists, exactly TWO arms and hands.
Anatomical RIGHT hand ALWAYS grips the sword hilt. Anatomical LEFT hand ALWAYS supports the black scabbard mouth at the hip. No hand swapping or two-handed blade grip. Same modestly long STRAIGHT slim silver blade and STRAIGHT black scabbard with silver fittings/red knot/tassel as reference, constant physical blade length. The sword is neither curved nor gigantic; a full unsheathed blade is roughly35percent of total character height. Only the part INSIDE the sheath may be hidden.
THE ATTACK MUST READ CLEARLY AS BOTTOM-TO-TOP. The striking blade moves from LOW near the forward knee, upward past waist and chest, then finishes HIGH beside/above the head. Never start by raising the sword and cutting downward. Do not simply reverse a downward slash animation. The sword is DRAWN while beginning the rising cut.
Frames0-3, first row: 0 exact approved partly-drawn ready stance; 1 gentle anticipation by lowering shoulders and bending knees a little, feet fixed; 2 rotate sheath mouth slightly down/front and lower sword hand toward the waist while drawing; 3 blade nearly clears scabbard at LOW hip height, right elbow natural, left hand pulls sheath a little behind hip. Blade tip stays LOW.
Frames4-7, second row, the RISING STRIKE: 4 full blade clears sheath, sword point LOW down-left near knee height, right hand low at hip; 5 upward cut starts, blade points outward-left at low waist level; 6 blade sweeps upward past chest, pointing upper-left about30degrees above horizontal while right forearm lifts; 7 finish the same rising arc with sword pointing STEEPLY UP-LEFT, tip ABOVE THE HAIR/TOP OF HEAD, right glove near upper chest/shoulder, elbow bent normally. Wrist stays connected to hilt, no stretched arm.
Frames8-11, third row: 8 brief high follow-through, blade tip STILL ABOVE HEAD, right hand lifted near shoulder; 9 settle in the same HIGH finishing pose with hair and coat lag; 10 begin CONTROLLED RECOVERY, bring right elbow down slightly while blade remains angled UP outside the face; 11 rotate the sword in a small controlled recovery arc in front of/outside the body, hand approaching waist, tip moving toward scabbard opening. This return is slower and relaxed, not a second attack. Show the complete sword continuously.
Frames12-15, last row: 12 sword tip aligns with black scabbard mouth, sword and sheath share a single straight centerline; 13 partway inserted; 14 mostly inserted; 15 exact ready pose matching frame0. Preserve right-hand-hilt and left-hand-scabbard roles throughout. The long sword NEVER disappears or flips from one side of its hilt to the other between adjacent frames. No ghost blades, smear/energy arcs, impact effects or extra equipment. Feet planted, no walking/jumping, no camera shift, no character size/head-width changes across frames. The visually dominant action is the LOW-TO-HIGH rising cut in frames4-8.

DIRECTION: FRONT VIEW ONLY, exactly like this reference. Chest and face keep facing the viewer throughout, with only subtle torso twist. Anatomical right arm is on SCREEN LEFT and left sheath hand SCREEN RIGHT. The rising cut travels up toward the character's SCREEN-LEFT side in front of the body, attacking the foreground. The high finishing sword is visible above the head to screen-left, outside the face; do not rotate the entire figure into side view. Maintain the reference face/hair silhouette/proportions uniformly across ALL16frames.

prompts.front_recovery_edit:
Precise localized correction of this EXISTING 4x4 sprite sheet. Keep the SAME canvas, same transparent background, same 16 cell positions, same character SCALE, head widths, faces, hair silhouettes, foot coordinates, clothing colors and rendering. Do not repaint or redesign the sheet. Preserve every pixel/shape of the FIRST THREE ROWS (frames0 through11): the upward-slashing attack is already CORRECT. Preserve last cell frame15 as well. ONLY repair the sword and sword-hand in the FIRST THREE CELLS of the BOTTOM/FOURTH ROW (frames12,13,14). Current error in these resheathing frames: a silver blade sticks out to the LEFT of the right-hand hilt while a second blade simultaneously connects that hand to the sheath on the RIGHT. It looks like a two-ended sword passing through the hand. REMOVE the wrong silver blade that sticks outward/up-left from the hilt in these three cells. A sword has one hilt, one guard and ONLY ONE blade extending from its guard toward the scabbard. The hand grips the short dark hilt on the left of the silver guard; the SOLE blade extends from that guard down-right into the black sheath mouth held by the other hand. There must be NO blade projecting from the butt end of the hilt!
Bottom-row cell1/frame12: align the sword point with the sheath mouth. Right hand (hilt hand) may extend modestly farther to screen LEFT of the belly with a naturally bent elbow to create space for the full silver blade. The ONE straight silver blade points DOWN-RIGHT from its hilt/guard, and its TIP meets the black scabbard opening held by the LEFT glove at the opposite hip. Show full straight blade BETWEEN the sword guard and the sheath mouth, on the same centerline as the scabbard. No silver blade on the outer-left side of the hilt; restore the original clean transparent background where that erroneous blade was.
Bottom-row cell2/frame13: partially slide that SAME blade INTO the black scabbard. Right hilt hand is closer to the left sheath hand; only the remaining silver blade segment between guard and sheath mouth remains visible. ALL the inserted blade is occluded by the black sheath. NO extra outward-left blade.
Bottom-row cell3/frame14: mostly inserted sword, returning to the original ready stance. A short exposed strip may remain between guard and sheath mouth as in frame15. No sword protruding from the hilt's butt or through the back of the scabbard.
In these3cells ONLY, minimal natural right elbow/wrist adjustment is allowed if needed. Keep right hand gripping hilt and left hand gripping sheath throughout, never switch hands, never add an extra glove or finger. Keep the same small arm proportions. The black sheath stays at the same hip and keeps its straight shape, length, red tassel and fittings. Preserve ALL HEAD/HAIR/FACE/BODY/LEGS pixels and proportions in these cells as closely as possible. No changes to the upward strike above, no new effects, no text, no palette/face/head-width drift. This is a small sword-geometry correction only, not new animation generation.
This is the FRONT VIEW sheet; keep it front-facing.
